ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In an isosceles triangle with a vertex angle of $36^\circ$, we refer to such a triangle as a "golden triangle", where the ratio of the base to the leg is the golden ratio. As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=36^\circ$, $AB=AC$, $BD$ bisects $\angle ABC$ and intersects $AC$ at point $D$. If $CD=1$, what is the length of $AC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle A=36^\circ$ and AB＝AC, with BD bisecting $\angle ABC$ and intersecting AC at point D,\\
it follows that $\angle ABC=\angle ACB=72^\circ$, $\angle A=\angle DBC=36^\circ$, and $\angle BCD=\angle BDC=72^\circ$,\\
implying that $\angle ACB=\angle BCD$,\\
which means $\triangle BCD\sim \triangle ABC$,\\
leading to the ratio BC$\colon$ AB=DC$\colon$ BC,\\
and given BC$\colon$ AB=$\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}$ and DC=1,\\
we find BC=$\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{2}$,\\
thus $\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{2}\colon$ AB=$\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}$,\\
resulting in AB=$\frac{\sqrt{5}+3}{2}$,\\
so AC=$\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{5}+3}{2}}$.

Reasoning: It is known that ∠A=36° and AB=AC, so the base angles ∠ABC=∠ACB=(180°-36°)/2=72°. BD bisects ∠ABC, therefore ∠DBC=36°. Because D is on AC, ∠BCD=∠BCA=72°. In △BCD, ∠BDC=180°-36°-72°=72°, so the angles of △BCD are 36°, 72°, 72°, and it is similar to △ABC. According to the corresponding relationship of similarity, there is BC/AB=CD/BC. In a golden triangle, the ratio of the base to the waist is BC/AB=(√5-1)/2. Also CD=1, so 1/BC=(√5-1)/2, obtaining BC=2/(√5-1)=(√5+1)/2. Then from BC/AB=(√5-1)/2, obtaining AB=BC·2/(√5-1)=((√5+1)/2)^2=(√5+3)/2. Since AB=AC, therefore AC=(√5+3)/2.
